slices.focus: Tasha takes a cabin trip without work laptop; clarifies preference for quiet, low-input travel
slices.summary: Tasha takes a short cabin trip with two novels and no work laptop — the first genuinely steady weekend in months. She reads slowly on the porch, takes one short walk, and feels no guilt about doing almost nothing. The experience clarifies that she strongly prefers quiet, low-input travel (cabins or coastal getaways) over city trips that require scheduling and energy. The agent helps her develop a personal travel rule (no work device, 1-2 loose anchors, reading that does not ask too much), start a small dedicated fund labeled 'cabin or coast,' and create a weekend home template (no laptop, one decent meal, one book, nowhere urgent to be). Tasha notices her jaw was not clenched, she was not scanning for the next thing, and she came home able to cook dinner — evidence the trip gave energy instead of taking it.
